races.paceDynamic: Traprain Law, Sans Bruit, Classic Maestro and Palacio will create a relentless early gallop with four confirmed front-runners in a small field. The soft ground at 2m½f will test stamina reserves as this quartet battle for position through the early stages. With only Matata, Calico, Le Nez Creux, Aeros Luck and Moudan sitting behind them, the pace will be honest throughout. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can capitalise on the expected pace collapse from over-racing leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners go too hard early and tie up from 3 out
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop will find out the leaders' stamina reserves on soft ground, allowing prominent racers with tactical speed to pick up the pieces. Horses like Matata and Calico who can track the pace without committing fully early will have the fitness edge late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Survivor
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders can dictate fractions and control the tempo
scenarios.body: Traprain Law or Palacio could use their class advantage to set sustainable fractions and kick clear when the others falter. Their recent soft ground form suggests they can handle the conditions better than their front-running rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even stronger than expected and all leaders stop
scenarios.body: Le Nez Creux coming back from a long break could benefit from the strongest possible gallop to set up his finishing kick. The Cromwell-trained horse has the class to capitalise if given the perfect setup from those in front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground plays slower than expected and one leader gets away
scenarios.body: Sans Bruit or Classic Maestro could steal a march if the ground doesn't take its toll as expected. This scenario requires the pace to be less punishing than the evidence suggests it will be.

races.paceDynamic: Milcree, Diamond Dealer, and Caughtinyourtrance will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with Big John Wayne likely to join the pace-forcing if needed. This quartet of confirmed front-runners will create a searching test of stamina over 3 miles on soft ground, with the pace likely to be honest throughout rather than stop-start. The relentless gallop will set up the race for the hold-up horses and those who can produce sustained finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and late closers who can capitalise on the expected pace collapse in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the four leaders go too hard and crack from 3f out
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop tells on the pace-setters as hold-up horses sweep past with fresh legs in the closing stages. Gamesters Guy, I Wish You, and Al Kalila are perfectly positioned to exploit the pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters moderate the gallop and stay competitive
scenarios.body: A more measured tempo allows some front-runners to stay in contention while prominent racers get the best of both worlds. Diamond Dealer and Califet En Vol can capitalise on their class advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter breaks clear and maintains the advantage
scenarios.body: Milcree or Diamond Dealer establish a commanding lead that the hold-up horses cannot peg back despite the strong pace. The winner comes from those who can sustain their effort from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop becomes unsustainably fast from the start
scenarios.body: All four leaders stop to a walk in the straight, creating chaos and allowing a mid-division runner to pick up the pieces. Just Over Land benefits from avoiding the early pace battle entirely.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Squirrel and Tellherthename will set a genuine pace from the off, with both confirmed leaders unlikely to compromise. The soft ground at 2m over hurdles will create a demanding test, while Tutti Quanti, Captain Hugo, Ooh Betty, Dedicated Hero and Welsh Charger all wanting prominent positions means inevitable congestion approaching the final two flights. This honest gallop combined with ground conditions will expose any weaknesses in stamina and jumping under pressure. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early traffic and produce late speed when others are stopping.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Collapse Late

scenarios.body: The genuine pace and soft conditions take their toll on the leaders, allowing closers with fresh legs to sweep past in the final furlong. Hold-up specialists like Gibbs Island and All In You are perfectly positioned to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace setters moderate their speed and prominent runners avoid traffic
scenarios.body: Captain Hugo and Tutti Quanti get ideal positions tracking the leaders without over-racing, then assert when the pace lifts approaching the last. Their class and tactical positioning proves decisive over the staying-on hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Patient
scenarios.trigger: If the six prominent runners create a wall and interfere with each other 2-3 out
scenarios.body: The bunching of so many forward-going types causes checking and lost momentum for those caught in the melee. Queenie St Clair and Gibbs Island, held up out the back, find clear runs down the outside to exploit the chaos.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wire-to-Wire Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Squirrel gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear at the last
scenarios.body: Jonathan Burke lets Secret Squirrel bowl along at his own rhythm without pressure, then the 7-year-old finds extra on the soft ground he handles well. The field leaves their runs too late to peg back the gutsy front-runner.

races.paceDynamic: Quebecois is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 21-runner Scottish Grand National, giving him a crucial tactical advantage to dictate terms without early pressure. With most others adopting prominent or hold-up styles, the pace is likely to be steady early before building through the middle stages as the field spreads out over Ayr's stamina-sapping 4m trip on testing soft ground. The large field and marathon distance will create natural attrition, with jumping errors and stamina failures likely to thin the pack significantly. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can secure good positions early and avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will plague hold-up horses in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quebecois Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Quebecois jumps cleanly and sets an even gallop without serious challenge for the lead.
scenarios.body: His uncontested front-running will allow him to conserve energy while others jostle for position behind, then he can kick clear when the pace lifts approaching the business end. The tactical advantage of controlling the race from the front proves decisive in this stamina test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes strong enough to blunt Quebecois's kick but not so fast as to set up the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: The prominent racers like Isaac Des Obeaux and Maximilian can track the pace without over-exerting, then have enough left to outstay the leader in the final furlong. Their superior class ratings shine through when positioned to strike.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and creates significant gaps, allowing a talented stayer to weave through.
scenarios.body: Montregard or King Of Answers can benefit from a truly-run race where the early leaders have gone too fast, but they need serious traffic luck through the field. Their class and finishing kick becomes effective only if the race sets up perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Creates Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers and mistakes eliminate the leading contenders, leaving the race wide open for a longshot.
scenarios.body: The sheer chaos of 21 runners over 4m on soft ground produces enough carnage to bring outsiders like Chasingouttheblues or Kap Vert into contention through avoiding trouble. Position and luck matter more than pure ability in this scenario.

scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Skerry Hill and Le Cold Grey fade early leaving a moderate tempo.
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical with a sprint finish, allowing the stronger finishers to come from behind and showcase their turn of foot. Hold-up horses get the easier lead they need to mount their challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Coconut Man or Jardin De Tunis gets a soft lead after rivals fade.
scenarios.body: The winner steals a march by dictating terms from the front, building an unassailable advantage that late closers cannot peg back. Front-running tactics prove decisive on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Scrimmaging
scenarios.trigger: If the four leaders interfere with each other early or stumble on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes stop-start with tactical positioning crucial, creating opportunities for patient hold-up horses to pick up the pieces. The race falls apart tactically, suiting those with the best finishing kicks.

watchPoints.text: Skerry Hill could be vulnerable after 169-day layoff despite his front-running style being ideal for dictating terms
Close House and Busted Springs are complete unknowns who could upset calculations if ready to win on debut
Brady Hartsfield's 4lb weight allowance could prove decisive in a competitive finish between the hold-up horses
The soft ground may deteriorate further given the race sequence, potentially favouring the most proven soft ground performers
Old Habits needs to overcome both fitness concerns and the strong early pace to showcase his proven class advantage
